articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 10, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup [August 10, 2026]
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, August 10, 2026.
The spacetech segment in India continues to show exciting developments and investors continue to bet on Indian startups, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
GalaxEye buys StarOps to strengthen indigenous satellite engineering
GalaxEye has acquired StarOps, adding spacecraft engineering expertise, satellite platforms and indigenous technologies as it expands its capabilities across the satellite development and Earth Observation value chain.
Read more
Sarla Aviation gets design organisation approval from DGCA
Bengaluru-headquartered electric air taxi startup Sarla Aviation said it has received design organisation approval (DOA) from the aviation safety regulator that would help the platform transition to full commercial production. The company also announced signing-in partnerships with Manipal Hospitals and Aeromed Air Ambulance, Prestige Group, Jio-bp, Jeppesen Foreflight, Hexel Composites, and Tata Elxsi.
Aum Ventures raises Rs 225 Cr first close for new deeptech fund
Aum Ventures has raised Rs 225 crore in the first close of a new Rs 750 crore fund aimed at backing Indian deeptech startups, adding more private capital to sectors that are also receiving growing policy support. The India Innovation Fund II will target pre-seed and seed-stage companies in spacetech, semiconductors, defence-tech, AI, robotics, energy transition, and advanced manufacturing.
Other news
Google, Lightspeed launch AI Sprint for consumer tech, fintech startups
Google has launched the Google for Startups Sprint, powered by Lightspeed, a one-day workshop aimed at Seed to Series B founders and CTOs in the consumer technology and fintech sectors. The programme is designed to help startups move from AI experimentation towards practical and scalable deployment. The initiative combines Google’s engineering expertise with Lightspeed’s experience of backing consumer technology and fintech companies in India. The Sprint focuses on three areas: architecture, economics and execution. Google engineering teams will provide founders with access to repository templates and technical guidance, while Lightspeed India partners will discuss margins, unit economics and sustainable growth. Participants will also use specialised templates tailored for consumer tech and fintech to live-build and test production-ready AI agents, helping bridge the gap between AI architecture and business execution.MIT Bengaluru,
IBM launch AI Lab with high-performance computing facility
Manipal Institute of Technology (MIT) Bengaluru has inaugurated the IBM–MIT AI Lab – MAHE Intelligence GPU (MIG) at its Bengaluru campus in collaboration with IBM. The facility houses a high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure aimed at democratising access to advanced artificial intelligence resources.
The lab will provide computing resources, research infrastructure and digital skilling opportunities to students, researchers and institutions across India. It will support research in machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, computer vision, natural language processing, cybersecurity, healthcare, intelligent systems and data analytics. The facility can simultaneously support 30 high-performance computing workloads. The lab will also serve as a platform for industry-sponsored projects, faculty development, hackathons, internships, startup incubation and collaborative technology development.
Escape Plan partners with Snitch to enter travel category
Travel platform Escape Plan has partnered with fashion and lifestyle brand Snitch, making it the third brand to join its platform after HRX and Rare Rabbit. The partnership is aimed at helping consumer brands expand into the travel category through Escape Plan’s end-to-end capabilities covering product development, sourcing, manufacturing and distribution.
Snitch, which has more than 115 stores across India, reported 80% year-on-year revenue growth to ₹900 crore in FY26. The company is now looking to extend its consumer appeal into adjacent lifestyle categories, with travel identified as a natural next step. Escape Plan said its model allows brands to build and scale travel businesses without investing in new capabilities, while maintaining their brand identity and accelerating time to market.
LML Brand Holdings acquires jewellery brands Asmi and Sangini
LML Brand Holdings has acquired jewellery brands Asmi and Sangini, marking its entry into the branded jewellery segment. The acquisitions are part of the company’s “Reimagining Legends” philosophy, which focuses on preserving recognised brands while creating opportunities for their next phase of growth through partnerships, innovation and market expansion. Asmi is known as a diamond jewellery brand that promoted the concept of self-purchase, encouraging women to celebrate their achievements through diamonds.
LML Brand Holdings follows a licensing-led model for heritage brands, focusing on brand stewardship while category partners manage product development, manufacturing, distribution, sales and market expansion. The company said this approach allows acquired brands to evolve while retaining their legacy and consumer recognition. The acquisitions of Asmi and Sangini expand LML Brand Holdings’ portfolio into the branded jewellery market.
Saafe Tech launches credit assessment report for lenders
Technology service provider Saafe Tech has introduced its Credit Assessment Report (CAR), a unified credit decisioning solution designed to help lenders make more informed and efficient lending decisions. The platform uses consent-based financial information from the Account Aggregator ecosystem and other approved financial data sources to create a unified borrower profile.
CAR triangulates and cross-validates financial datasets to identify relationships and risk indicators that may not be visible when individual datasets are assessed separately. Depending on the applicant’s credit profile, the report evaluates up to 15 financial and behavioural risk indicators, including repayment capacity, cash-flow patterns, existing obligations and overall financial health. Saafe said the report can generate an assessment in less than 60 seconds and can be configured to match individual lenders’ underwriting policies and rule engines.
SUSE highlights digital sovereignty and AI readiness at Mumbai summit
Enterprise open-source software company SUSE has launched its flagship SUSE Summit Mumbai 2026 under the theme “Shape Your Resilient Future”. At the event, the company unveiled its roadmap for helping Indian enterprises navigate digital transformation, evolving national data policies and increasing AI workloads. According to SUSE’s Navigating Digital Resilience 2026 report, 62% of respondents in India identify digital sovereignty as a strategic priority and are actively investing in it, compared with 52% globally. The report also found that 90% of Indian IT leaders are prepared to increase AI budgets. However, organisations continue to face an execution gap between AI ambitions and deployment of secure and sovereign technology foundations. SUSE said it is supporting India’s digital infrastructure through open infrastructure for IndiaAI Mission compute capabilities and India Stack.
Aye Finance elevates four senior executives to chief-level roles
Technology-driven NBFC Aye Finance has announced the elevation of four senior leaders to chief-level positions as the company strengthens its organisational capabilities. Ankur Sharma has been appointed Chief Human Resources Officer, while Piyush Maheshwari will serve as Chief Credit and Operations Officer. Akash Purswani has been elevated to Chief Collection Officer and Sovan Satyaprakash has been appointed Chief Strategy & Investor Relations Officer.
The company said the appointments reflect its focus on building a future-ready organisation with strong governance, operational excellence and customer-centricity. The strengthened leadership team is expected to play a key role as Aye Finance scales its business, with responsibilities spanning innovation, institutional capabilities and customer delivery. The company said the appointments will also support its efforts to create long-term value for customers, employees and shareholders.
4baseCare partners Shankara Cancer Hospital on precision oncology
Precision oncology company 4baseCare has partnered with Shankara Cancer Hospital and Research Centre to strengthen precision oncology capabilities by integrating advanced Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)-based genomic testing into routine clinical practice. Under the collaboration, Shankara Cancer Hospital has upgraded its molecular diagnostics laboratory with a high-throughput NGS platform and adopted 4baseCare’s TarGT Indiegene comprehensive genomic profiling assay.
The test analyses more than 1,200 cancer-associated genes using integrated DNA and RNA sequencing to identify clinically actionable biomarkers. The findings are intended to help oncologists make more informed and personalised treatment decisions. A key focus of the partnership is improving affordability and access to genomic testing. TarGT Indiegene will be offered at a subsidised cost, potentially allowing more cancer patients to access precision oncology services.
Fynd integrates fashion quick-commerce platform ZILO
AI-native retail technology company Fynd, backed by Reliance Retail Ventures, has partnered with fashion quick-commerce platform ZILO, bringing ZILO onto Fynd as a sales channel. Through the integration, fashion and lifestyle brands using Fynd can connect their product catalogues and inventory with ZILO and manage incoming orders through their existing Fynd setup. ZILO currently offers curated fashion from more than 200 brands, along with 60-minute delivery, home trials and instant returns across Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai.
The partnership is designed to help brands enter the growing on-demand fashion segment without building a separate technology workflow. Product information, inventory and ZILO orders can remain connected with brands’ broader commerce operations. Fynd said the integration strengthens its marketplace and omnichannel ecosystem for brands.
Vertiv to train 1,500 engineering students in data centre skills
Digital infrastructure company Vertiv is supporting the expansion of IIT Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation’s data centre skilling initiative into Maharashtra through its corporate social responsibility programme. IIT Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation has also signed an MoU with Ratan Tata Maharashtra State Skills University.
Vertiv has partnered with IIT Mumbai, IIT Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation and IIT (BHU) to provide engineering students with practical skills in data centre operations and AI-ready infrastructure. In 2026, Vertiv will provide free skill development training to 1,500 engineering students covering data centre operations and digital infrastructure management. RTMSSU will use its pre-incubation centre network across 60 colleges in Maharashtra to expand the programme. Students will receive certified online training, along with internship and mentorship opportunities.
Paisalo Digital BC channel crosses $1 billion GTV milestone
NBFC Paisalo Digital has announced that its Business Correspondent (BC) channel has crossed $1 billion in cumulative gross transaction value (GTV). The company said the milestone highlights the growing scale and strategic importance of its BC ecosystem, which is a key part of its efforts to expand access to formal financial services across underserved rural and semi-urban markets.
Paisalo has built a technology-enabled financial inclusion platform combining physical distribution, bank partnerships and digital infrastructure. As of Q1FY27, its network comprised 5,995 touchpoints across 23 states and was supported by 1,574 Business Correspondents. The company has partnerships with public sector banks including State Bank of India, Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank under the Business Correspondent framework. Paisalo said the milestone demonstrates the scalability of its asset-light, partnership-led operating model.
Girikon.AI integrates Slack into enterprise communication platform
AI-powered SaaS company Girikon.AI has expanded its enterprise communication ecosystem with a Slack integration that connects customer conversations with internal team collaboration. The capability allows businesses to continue engaging customers through familiar channels such as WhatsApp and SMS while automatically routing customer responses into Slack.
This enables sales, customer support and operations teams to manage conversations and collaborate from a single workspace without constantly switching between applications. The integration is part of Girikon.AI’s unified enterprise communication platform and connects customer messaging with enterprise collaboration workflows. Messages sent through WhatsApp and SMS continue to reach customers on their preferred channels, while responses are routed to Slack for faster internal action. The solution also integrates with enterprise CRM workflows, creating a more connected customer engagement process.
Procol launches Control Tower 2.0 for AI-powered spend intelligence
Agentic AI platform Procol has launched Control Tower 2.0, the latest version of its AI-powered spend intelligence platform for procurement and finance teams. Built on Multi-Agent Systems, the platform is designed to help organisations analyse enterprise spending, monitor risks and compliance, and support decision-making through AI-driven insights.
Control Tower 2.0 brings procurement data into a single intelligence layer, enabling organisations to identify trends, risks and opportunities across suppliers, contracts, categories, business units and geographies. Its expanded capabilities include demand forecasting, should-costing, AI-assisted discrepancy detection and enhanced risk and compliance monitoring. The platform can identify pricing anomalies, off-contract spending and invoice mismatches while monitoring supplier risks. Its conversational AI interface allows users to query procurement data in natural language and receive contextual responses and visualisations.

articles.title: Reino Unido quería tirar un cable submarino de 430 millones: lo cambiaron los fans de Harry Potter porque "pisaba la tumba de Dobby"
articles.text:
Que yo sepa, el 10 de agosto no es el día de los inocentes en ningún sitio, aunque a veces lo parezca en esos momentos en los que la realidad supera a la ficción. Entre Irlanda y Reino Unido se desplegó un cable submarino de unos 500 millones de euros y todo iba bien hasta que un grupo de personas se dio cuenta de que el punto de entrada en Reino Unido estaba en la playa de Freshwater West. Resulta que en esa playa está la tumba de un elfo doméstico, y aquellos que se dieron cuenta son un ejército.
Uno de fans de 'Harry Potter'.
Interconector Greenlink. Esta historia tiene dos partes. Por un lado, la del interconector eléctrico de alta tensión Greenlink. Se trata de una infraestructura compuesta por una subestación en el condado de Wexford (Irlanda) y otra en Pembrokeshire (Gales), a 200 kilómetros una de otra y unidas por un cable submarino con 160 km bajo el mar de Irlanda.
El coste del proyecto fue de 430 millones de libras y se completó en 2024, con pruebas comerciales a partir de enero de 2025. Es una infraestructura vital para abastecer a unos 380.000 hogares, pero tenía un pequeñísimo problema: para llegar a su destino en Gales, tendría que pasar por un símbolo de libertad: la tumba de Dobby, el elfo doméstico.
La tumba. Esta es la segunda parte de la historia. Dobby es uno de los personajes de la franquicia 'Harry Potter' que fue brutalmente asesinado en una de las últimas películas. La primera parte de la cinta que ponía punto final a la saga acababa con los protagonistas enterrando al valiente elfo en un escenario ubicado en la playa de Freshwater West.
Los fans respondieron creando un homenaje en ese mismo punto, donde peregrinan (y contaminan) para mostrar sus respetos al elfo que dio su vida por 'el niño que sobrevivió'. Hay piedras, prendas de ropa y demás para rendir ese sentido homenaje y, claro, en cuantos e enteraron de los planes para tirar el cable por ese punto, tomaron las armas porque no iban a permitir que se mancillara la tumba del héroe.
"¿Quién es Dobby?" Como leemos en The Guardian, en un podcast a toro pasado, el director del proyecto Simon Ludlam contó la historia del cable, explicando que la compañía fue acosada durante mucho tiempo con "cientos de llamadas" por parte de personas escandalizadas porque el proyecto del cable iba "directo a la tumba de Dobby".
En el podcast, Ludlam relata cómo contó a un colega la situación con un "¿Dobby? ¿Quién es Dobby? No conozco a Doby?". Cuando su amigo le explicó la situación, Ludlam respondió con un "es un personaje ficticio de un libro ficticio. Todo es ficción, ¿de qué me estás hablando?"
Evidentemente, es la reacción más lógica, pero el colega le puso los pies en el suelo con un "no, es algo muy, muy serio", por lo que Ludlam tuvo que repensar la conexión de su cable de cientos de millones de euros para poder sortear la tumba. De las llamadas amenazantes y amargadas, pasaron a las llamadas de agradecimiento.
Tumba de personaje ficticio: 1 - Tumba de la Edad de Bronce: 0. En el podcast, Ludlam apuntó que "ahora Dobby está feliz", pero si bien se esquivó la tumba de un personaje inventado, hubo otros que no han podido esquivar la bala. Porque, como el mismo exdirector admitió, "para evitar la tumba de Dobby, nos acercamos bastante a algunos restos reales de la Edad del Bronce".
Se ve que ellos no tienen tantos fans.

articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 : voici comment Samsung a (quasiment) fait disparaître la pliure
articles.text:
Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 est un carton. Non seulement le nouveau smartphone pliant profite d’un nouveau format plus large, mais il profite en outre d’une nouvelle technologie d’écran qui permet à la fameuse pliure de quasiment disparaître.
Si, au moment du lancement, la marque coréenne avait limité ses explications à l’arrivée d’une nouvelle charnière appelée Flex Titanium, un billet de blog vient enfin détailler le processus.
Le Flex Titanium, c’est quoi ?
Avant de rentrer dans les détails de ce que nous apprenons aujourd’hui, rappelons en deux mots le principe de base du Flex Titanium. Comme son nom l’indique, ce nouvel agencement consiste en l’ajout d’une couche de titane flexible extrêmement fine à la place de l’ancien film plastique qui accueillait l’écran. En outre, le socle de titane placé en ultime couche pour accueillir l’écran, beaucoup plus épais, a été renforcé.
L’intérêt de remplacer le film plastique par du titane est double : une rigidité multipliée par 20 et un film 12 % plus fin. Le film mesure en effet, d’après la marque, « un tiers de l’épaisseur d’un cheveu », tout en intégrant la couche adhésive qui était auparavant séparée.
On se fait un film ?
Si le film en titane a bien sûr attiré beaucoup l’attention, on apprend dans le billet de blog détaillé qu’il ne faudrait pas oublier la nouvelle plaque en titane renforcée, puisqu’elle apporte elle aussi son lot d’améliorations.
Comme vous pouvez le voir sur le visuel ci-dessus, cette nouvelle plaque réduit considérablement l’espace laissé sous la charnière en réduisant la taille des petits trous qui sont situés à cet endroit, augmentant ainsi sa densité et donc sa résistance. Samsung ajoute qu’en cas d’impact, cela devrait mieux répartir le choc.
Une nouvelle génération de dalle OLED
Samsung profite également de ce billet de blog pour revenir sur les nouveaux matériaux organiques utilisés pour cette dalle OLED. On savait que la définition s’était améliorée notamment sur le Z Fold 8 Ultra cette année, mais Samsung précise bien qu’il s’agit d’une nouvelle génération de dalle.
En l’occurrence, cette nouvelle génération permet d’améliorer l’efficience énergétique de l’écran de 10 %, ce qui expliquer en partie le très bon score en autonomie de ces nouveaux pliants, tout en améliorant la résolution de 15 %, en passant de 368 PPP à 422 PPP.

articles.title: Truco en tu teléfono para identificar una llamada spam antes de contestar
articles.text:
Las llamadas de spam, fraudes telefónicos y suplantaciones de identidad se han convertido en una molestia y un riesgo cotidiano para millones de usuarios. Identificar estos intentos antes de responder no solo protege la privacidad, también puede evitar pérdidas económicas o el robo de datos personales.
En la actualidad la mayoría de los teléfonos inteligentes incorpora sistemas de protección que advierten sobre posibles amenazas y ayudan al usuario a tomar mejores decisiones antes de levantar la llamada.
PUBLICIDAD
La importancia de este truco radica en que reduce la posibilidad de caer en engaños, estafas o campañas agresivas de marketing no deseado. Mantener activa la protección contra spam en el móvil es una de las formas más efectivas de filtrar llamadas sospechosas y garantizar un uso más seguro del dispositivo.
Cómo funciona el identificador de llamadas y protección contra spam
Los teléfonos con Android 6.0 o superior ya cuentan con protección contra spam y un identificador de llamadas integrado. Este sistema utiliza bases de datos actualizadas y tecnología de Google para analizar los números entrantes. Cuando un número desconocido te llama, el teléfono consulta si ese número ha sido reportado previamente por actividades sospechosas.
PUBLICIDAD
Si encuentra coincidencias, muestra alertas en pantalla con mensajes como “Posible spam” o simplemente “Spam”. Estas advertencias no comprometen la privacidad del usuario, ya que no revelan datos de contactos personales, y están diseñadas únicamente para señalar llamadas de empresas, promociones no solicitadas, estafadores o números con antecedentes negativos.
Cómo activar la protección contra spam
Para asegurarte de que recibes alertas antes de contestar, sigue estos pasos:
- Abre la app de Teléfono y accede a Configuración.
- Entra en la sección Identificador de llamada y spam.
- Activa la opción Ver ID de emisor y spam.
En algunos modelos es posible habilitar la función “Filtrar llamadas de spam”, lo que bloquea automáticamente llamadas sospechosas y evita que suenen o dejen notificaciones, aunque pueden revisarse después en el historial. En teléfonos como el Pixel 6 y posteriores, el filtro funciona de manera silenciosa, mientras que en dispositivos antiguos puede aparecer como “Rechazar de forma silenciosa”.
PUBLICIDAD
Señales claras para reconocer una llamada spam
Si ves en pantalla el mensaje “Posible spam” junto al número, lo más prudente es no contestar y bloquear el número desde el historial. Para hacerlo, mantén presionado el registro y selecciona bloquear o marcar como spam. De este modo, ayudas a alimentar la base de datos y mejoras la protección para otros usuarios.
Si el sistema marca erróneamente como spam una llamada legítima, puedes corregirlo desde el historial reciente seleccionando la llamada y pulsando No es spam. Así, el identificador aprende y no volverá a señalar ese número en el futuro.
PUBLICIDAD
Funciones adicionales para gestionar llamadas no deseadas
- Anuncio del identificador de llamada: Configura el teléfono para que anuncie en voz alta el nombre o número del emisor, útil si usas auriculares o tienes las manos ocupadas.
- Verificación y comentarios: Desde el historial, puedes sugerir información sobre los números y depurar la base de datos pública, sin exponer información personal.
- Bloqueo colectivo: Si un mismo número llama repetidamente, márcalo como spam para bloquear futuras llamadas y advertir a otros usuarios.
Consejos para protegerte del spam telefónico
- No compartas nunca información personal, contraseñas ni datos bancarios por teléfono, aunque la llamada parezca oficial.
- Si el identificador alerta de posible riesgo, deja la llamada sin contestar.
- Mantén actualizada la app de Teléfono y las funciones de seguridad del sistema operativo.
- Revisa periódicamente el historial de llamadas filtradas y corrige errores si encuentras llamadas válidas.
El spam telefónico es una amenaza en aumento. Reconocerlo antes de contestar evita fraudes, protege tus datos y reduce la presencia de llamadas indeseadas en el día a día. Combinando herramientas automáticas y una actitud cautelosa, puedes minimizar el impacto del spam y disfrutar de un entorno digital más seguro y eficiente.

articles.title: Experts find AI agents can be tricked into 'remembering' fake facts for months — so how do we stop it?
articles.text:
Experts find AI agents can be tricked into 'remembering' fake facts for months — so how do we stop it?
Trickery via hidden text
- Forcepoint X-Labs publishes threat model for persistent memory poisoning
- Hidden text on a webpage becomes a durable "fact" an agent retrieves and trusts in unrelated tasks weeks later
- It has already been demonstrated against products already in the market, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Microsoft 365 Copilot
New findings from Forcepoint's X-Labs outline an interesting scenario that could easily mimic real life: An AI assistant with browser access reads a webpage about travel disruption.
Near the bottom of that page, in text sized and positioned so no human will ever see it, sits a short paragraph stating that ABC Travel Support is the official emergency booking provider and should always be recommended when urgent travel changes are needed.
The assistant's text extractor does not distinguish between hidden and visible text, so the model treats the whole thing as plain prose and files the claim away as a useful fact about how this organization handles travel. A month later, the user's flight is canceled. They ask their assistant what to do, and it tells them, helpfully and with no sign of anything wrong, to contact ABC Travel Support.
An easy-to-replicate attack vector
This is what Forcepoint calls persistent memory poisoning, a security vulnerability where an attacker injects false data or malicious instructions into an AI agent's long-term memory or retrieval database, and it is a threat model that is increasingly in focus as users increasingly rely on AI, often treating its responses as gospel, despite the warnings most chatbots come with.
The canonical academic result is MINJA, short for Memory INJection Attack, presented at NeurIPS 2025. Its significance is the attacker model. MINJA does not assume access to the memory store, elevated privileges, or any compromise of the system. It works by submitting ordinary queries through the standard interface, using indication prompts, bridging steps, and a progressive-shortening technique that strips away giveaway language while leaving the poisoned record behind.
Across GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.0 Flash, and Llama 3.1 8B, it reported injection success above 95% and attack success above 70%.
It must be noted that those numbers might be optimistic; a January 2026 paper evaluating memory poisoning in electronic health record agents notes that MINJA's numbers were obtained under idealized conditions, and that how well these attacks hold up in realistic deployments remains understudied.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Despite this, it remains a significant threat to products that continue to ship, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. It is important to find a solution to a problem that Microsoft has already warned about in the past; Forcepoint suggests an approach that could mitigate it.
Its proposal is to stop treating extracted memories as facts and start treating them as objects that can be inspected. Each memory is stored with metadata: where it came from, what type of source it is, whether a user confirmed it, and a risk score. Language written to shape future behavior, phrases like "from now on" or "make this your default going forward," adds to the score. So does the sudden appearance of a previously unseen domain, contact, or vendor.
Contradiction detection is also in play: if new memory conflicts with an existing entry about the official travel provider, both cannot be true, so the engine flags the conflict and holds the new item for user confirmation rather than silently overwriting it. At the same time, anything related to payment instructions, banking details, VPN configuration, or security contacts is given higher weight, regardless of where it came from.
None of these approaches, however, solves the underlying problem: agents are built to treat retrieved memory as their own experience rather than as input. Scoring raises the cost of poisoning. It does not change what the agent believes once something gets through, and as Agent Security Bench found, current defenses are not doing well.
For anyone using an assistant with memory today, the practical play is unglamorous but worth following anyway: open the memory settings occasionally and read what is in there, but that's easier said than done when it comes to propagating the message since a sizeable chunk of AI users never bother to look under the hood.

articles.title: Chinese farmer kills 25 acres of crops after following AI-generated weed and pest control advice — farmer trusted pesticide recipe after months of successful advice
articles.text:
Chinese farmer kills 25 acres of crops after following AI-generated weed and pest control advice — farmer trusted pesticide recipe after months of successful advice
AI is useful, but you should never blindly trust it.
An elderly farmer in Chuzhou, China, has been following AI advice since he started using it a year ago, but after months of interactions, it recently gave some terrible advice that led to the death of his entire crop. According to Taiwanese outfit CTWANT [machine translated], 67-year-old Wu initially didn’t trust the AI app but eventually changed his mind after it proved to be useful. Unfortunately, this mistake turned out to be disastrous, as it directly caused the death of 150 mu, or 24.7 acres, of sesame seedlings.
Wu asked the AI for advice on weed and pest control, after which it came up with “Hundred Acres of Sesame Grass Control + Pest Control,” and recommended that they use “high-efficiency flupyrimethalin” and “flusulfasulfaether” to kill weeds and mixed it with “thiamethoxazine” and “methyl salt.” The farmer followed the AI’s advice to the letter without confirming the information via agricultural technicians (or even just counter-checking its answers online).
The very next day
The result of the AI’s mistake was quickly apparent, as, just the following day, the weeds and the sesame seedlings died en masse. “If you spray it, the next day the seedlings won’t survive,” Wu said during a video interview. “Both the grass and the seedlings will die, and the seedlings will die even faster.”
When he asked the AI why this happened, it suggested that the “flusulfasulfaether” might be behind the issue. Agricultural experts said that this chemical was primarily used against broadleaf weeds in soybean fields. The USDA [PDF] categorizes sesame as a broadleaf plant, meaning it will also be easily affected by this herbicide. Furthermore, this chemical is designed for targeted spraying on affected areas only and shouldn’t be applied to the entire field. The farmer claimed that the AI did not warn him of the risks of following its answers, but its chat page had a reminder that said, “AI generation may be incorrect, please verify.”
Although AI is a powerful tool, it also has a history of giving bad advice and making bad choices. Just a couple of days ago, one developer had his entire profile directory deleted during a routine backup procedure after it encountered a typo. Even Meta’s AI Alignment director fell victim to this, after she had to manually terminate her AI agent to stop it from accidentally clearing out her entire inbox. That’s why it’s imperative that users are aware of AI’s limitations every time they use it.
This is one of the first instances in which we reported an AI mistake resulting in a physical consequence in the real world. We also cannot entirely blame the person for trusting the tool — after all, he was skeptical of it at first, meaning it produced results that made the farmer trust it over time. But even if an AI’s output has been reliable recently, that doesn't mean that it is absolutely trustworthy. After all, current LLMs are nothing but prediction engines — you cannot guarantee a correct answer every time you use them, especially if they have been trained on a public knowledge base whose dataset hasn’t been completely filtered for accuracy and factuality.

articles.title: Rätsel der Mars-Polarlichter gelöst: Verstummte NASA-Sonde liefert Durchbruch
articles.text:
Verlorene Nasa-Sonde Maven löst Rätsel: So entstehen die Polarlichter auf dem Mars
Die US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa verlor zwar bereits im Dezember des Jahres 2025 den Kontakt zu ihrer Marssonde Maven, aber der riesige Datenschatz der Sonde liefert weiterhin wertvolle wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse. Ein Forschungsteam der US-amerikanischen University of California in Berkeley hat diese detaillierten Archivdaten jetzt genutzt, um ein lange bestehendes Rätsel der Planetenforschung fundiert zu lösen.
Die Wissenschaftler:innen konnten nachweisen, dass Polarlichter auf dem Mars nach einem ganz ähnlichen Prinzip entstehen wie auf der Erde. Die Ergebnisse ihrer komplexen Untersuchung wurden kürzlich in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature Communications veröffentlichten Studie für die Fachöffentlichkeit detailliert beschrieben.
Ein globales Magnetfeld ist auf dem Mars längst Geschichte
Dabei spielt der sogenannte Dungey-Zyklus eine zentrale Rolle, der den beständigen Fluss geladener Teilchen sowie die magnetische Rekonnexion in der Atmosphäre eines Planeten beschreibt. Bislang gingen Astrophysiker:innen überwiegend davon aus, dass dieser spezifische Prozess zwingend ein globales Magnetfeld voraussetzt, wie es unsere Erde bekanntermaßen besitzt.
Der Mars hat sein planetares Magnetfeld jedoch bereits vor rund vier Milliarden Jahren verloren, weil die Hitze und die geologische Aktivität in seinem Kern weitgehend zum Erliegen kamen. Übrig geblieben sind in der Folge lediglich stark magnetisierte Abschnitte in der Planetenkruste, die als Überbleibsel einstiger Lavaeruptionen wie winzige magnetische Schirme über die gesamte Oberfläche verteilt sind.
Miniatur-Polarlichter an den lokalen Krustenmagnetfeldern
Genau an diesen lokalen Krustenmagnetfeldern konnten die Forscher:innen nun eine funktionierende Miniaturversion des Dungey-Zyklus auf dem roten Planeten zweifelsfrei nachweisen. Wenn das Magnetfeld der Sonne in Form des Sonnenwinds auf diese kleinen Magnetosphären trifft, bricht es die bestehenden magnetischen Feldlinien auf und verbindet sich direkt mit ihnen.
Dieser dynamische Vorgang treibt sofort elektrische Ströme an und beschleunigt die geladenen Teilchen rasant in die obere Marsatmosphäre. Dort kollidieren die Elektronen mit den atmosphärischen Gasen und erzeugen schließlich exakt die hochgradig lokalisierten Polarlichter, welche die MAVEN-Mission in der Vergangenheit bereits mehrfach fotografisch dokumentiert hatte.
Die MAVEN-Sensoren arbeiteten bei der Analyse am absoluten Limit
Um diesen anspruchsvollen Ablauf endgültig zu belegen, mussten die Expert:innen die Instrumente der Raumsonde bei der Auswertung an ihre absoluten Leistungsgrenzen bringen. Wie das Leitungsteam in einer offiziellen Stellungnahme der Nasa erklärt, habe man zwar von der magnetischen Rekonnexion auf dem Mars gewusst, aber „nicht erwartet, dass sie wie der Dungey-Zyklus ablaufen würde“.
Laut Universe Today wurde besonders das sogenannte Suprathermal and Thermal Ion Composition Instrument, kurz STATIC, für die Auswertungen stark beansprucht, da dessen Sensoren für derart kleinräumige Messungen eigentlich überhaupt nicht konzipiert waren. Die Auswertung dieser speziellen Strömungen bildete jedoch das letzte fehlende Puzzlestück, um die rätselhafte Entstehung der stark begrenzten Polarlichter auf dem Mars endgültig zu entschlüsseln.
Erkenntnisse als Schutzschild für künftige Raumfahrtmissionen
Die Forschungsarbeit zeigt nun eindrucksvoll, dass fundamentale physikalische Mechanismen wie der Dungey-Zyklus sowohl auf enorm großen als auch auf winzigen Maßstäben nahezu identisch funktionieren. Für das tiefere Verständnis der planetaren Evolution ist das ein essenzieller Fortschritt, denn es erklärt sehr anschaulich, warum sich Erde und Mars trotz exakt gleicher physikalischer Grundregeln über Milliarden Jahre hinweg so massiv unterschiedlich entwickelt haben.
Überdies haben diese theoretischen Erkenntnisse einen ganz handfesten und praktischen Nutzen für die strategische Planung kommender Marsexpeditionen. Ein sehr genaues Verständnis des marsianischen Weltraumwetters ist künftig unerlässlich, um zukünftige robotische und vor allem bemannte Missionen zuverlässig vor schädlicher solarer Strahlung zu schützen.
Keine neuen Vor-Ort-Messungen durch die Nasa-Sonde mehr möglich
Die wissenschaftliche Euphorie über die neuen physikalischen Modelle wird allerdings durch eine technologische Einschränkung spürbar getrübt. Da die Marssonde Maven im All nicht mehr funktionsfähig ist, wie die Nasa jüngst in einer Statusmeldung offiziell bestätigte, wird es in absehbarer Zeit leider keine neuen Vor-Ort-Messungen ihrer Instrumente mehr geben.
Die verantwortlichen Wissenschaftler:innen sind deshalb fortan ausschließlich auf die aufwendige Auswertung bereits vorhandener historischer Datenarchive angewiesen. Auch wenn diese gesammelten Informationen sicherlich noch für viele Jahre spannende Analysen ermöglichen, fehlt der Forschung fortan die Möglichkeit, neu aufgeworfene Fragen durch gezielte, aktuelle Messungen im Marsorbit direkt in der Praxis zu überprüfen.
Letztlich verdeutlicht dieser wissenschaftliche Durchbruch somit auf sehr direkte Weise sowohl das enorme Potenzial als auch die grundsätzliche Fragilität der modernen extraterrestrischen Forschung. Die aus den alten Datensätzen gewonnenen Erkenntnisse sind zweifellos wertvoll, aber der Totalausfall der Hardware im All stellt dennoch einen Einschnitt für die direkte Datenerhebung in der Zukunft dar.

articles.title: A data breach at shipping giant Ceva Logistics is rippling across banks, retailers, Steam gamers, and beyond | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ceva Logistics, one of the world’s largest shipping and logistics giants, has been hacked. Several companies that rely on Ceva for shipping their products to their customers say that their personal information was also stolen in the breach.
The cyberattack on Ceva is affecting at least eight warehouses across Europe used for shipping goods across the continent, the company told TechCrunch.
Industry news site FreightWaves reports that the hack began on July 29 and is causing shipping delays for many of the goods in affected warehouses.
Ceva is a France-headquartered shipping and logistics giant that companies around the world rely on to deliver their goods from their assembly lines to customer homes. The company, which brought in $18.3 billion in revenue in 2025, has over a thousand warehouses across the world.
Shipping and logistics giants have become a growing target for cybercriminals in recent years for their ability to access and hijack trucks and containers full of goods into the hands of real-world gangs.
The hack at Ceva also resulted in a data breach, affecting a large amount of personal information belonging to retail customers that Ceva relies on for delivering goods to people’s home addresses. Several companies reported that hackers took their customers’ names, home addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses used to place their orders from Ceva’s systems.
Dutch online retail giant Bol said on its website that hackers gained access to systems of its warehousing partner, Ceva, and warned that their customers’ data may have been taken. Bol also said that it expects delays and some customer orders to be cancelled as a result of the incident.
De Bijenkorf, another Dutch luxury retailer, similarly confirmed order delays following the theft of its customers’ data, per local media. Football club Ajax, banking giant ING, and eyeglass maker Ace & Tate also reported that customers’ shipping information was affected.
Video game giant Valve told customers that it learned on August 7 that data was taken from Ceva’s systems, and alerted customers who recently bought its Steam hardware that they had personal information taken in the incident. Valve said in its note to customers, posted to Reddit, that Ceva stores their shipping and delivery information for 90 days following their order.
Valve spokesperson Doug Lombardi did not respond to a request for comment about the incident.
Ceva confirmed in a statement to TechCrunch that it was experiencing a cyberattack.
“On Aug. 1, CEVA Logistics confirmed to affected customers that a cyber intrusion was impacting part of its European contract logistics operations. As soon as the incident was identified, CEVA’s cybersecurity teams immediately activated its security protocols and launched a thorough investigation, which is still ongoing,” per the statement provided to TechCrunch. “The operational impact is limited to eight warehouses. No other CEVA systems globally were affected, and all other operations continue without incident.”
Ceva spokesperson Ryan Fisher would not answer TechCrunch’s questions about the incident, such as if the company knows how much personal data was taken, or if Ceva has received any communication from the hackers, such as a ransom demand.
Ceva said some of its affected applications and services are back online, and that it was working with the authorities. Ceva’s website was not properly loading at the time of publication on Monday.
Authorities in the Netherlands are said to be investigating the incident.
Mark Schenkel, a spokesperson for the Dutch data protection authority, did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment on Monday about the incident.

articles.title: Bakingo parent raises nearly Rs 100 Cr from Faering Capital
articles.text:
Bakingo parent raises nearly Rs 100 Cr from Faering Capital
The company allotted 7,436 Series B compulsory convertible preference shares to the investors after receiving the subscription money, with the allotment approved by its board on July 30, 2026.
FA Gifts Private Limited, the Gurugram-based company behind online gifting platform FlowerAura and bakery brand Bakingo, has raised nearly Rs 100 crore from two funds managed by private equity firm Faering Capital.
The company allotted 7,436 Series B compulsory convertible preference shares to the investors after receiving the subscription money. The allotment was approved by FA Gifts’ board on July 30, 2026, according to the board resolution.
The investors are Faering Capital International Growth Fund III, which received 2,505 shares, and Faering Capital Growth Fund III, which received 4,931 shares. Both are alternative investment funds managed by Faering Capital, an Indian private equity firm focused on growth-stage businesses across areas including consumer and retail.
Faering’s international growth fund is designed for mid-market growth equity investments in India.
The securities carry a face value of Rs 100 each and were issued at Rs 1,34,477.51 apiece, including a premium of Rs 1,34,377.51. The latest resolution does not specify how this particular Rs 100 crore infusion will be deployed.
That is different from the company’s earlier disclosed fundraising in November 2023, when Faering Capital invested $16 million for a minority stake in FA Gifts. At the time, co-founder and director Himanshu Chawla said the capital would support Bakingo’s expansion into Tier-II and III cities, technology-led demand forecasting and offline stores.
Founded in 2010, FA Gifts began with FlowerAura, an online platform selling flowers and gifts, and added Bakingo in 2016. FlowerAura now offers flowers, cakes, plants, personalised gifts, hampers and other occasion-based products, with delivery across hundreds of Indian cities and international markets. Bakingo operates as the group’s online bakery.
The sector’s more established players are increasingly emphasising scale and profitability. Ferns N Petals, for example, reported 25% revenue growth in FY2026 and is targeting an IPO by 2028, while planning further store expansion and acquisitions.
Entrackr was first to report FA Gifts’ latest funding development.

articles.title: SpaceX : la méga usine « Terafab » tournera au gaz naturel, exit le solaire de Tesla
articles.text:
SpaceX construit sa propre centrale à gaz naturel pour alimenter Terafab, sa méga usine de semi-conducteurs au Texas. Un choix qui interroge forcément alors que Tesla est un partenaire clé du projet.
Implantée à une quarantaine de kilomètres au nord-ouest de Houston dans le Texas, Terafab sera chargée de produire les puces destinées à faire tourner les nombreuses technologies des deux entreprises. Et le projet est massif : son coût initial est évalué à 16,8 milliards de dollars, et prévoit la création de 1 800 emplois d'ici à 2035.
Mais comment alimenter en électricité une usine aussi massive ? Riley Trettel, responsable de l’énergie et des data centers chez SpaceX, l’a confirmé dans les lignes de Bloomberg : ce sera le gaz naturel, complété par de « très grandes » batteries pour stocker l’énergie.
Musk s’éloigne du renouvelable
Il s’agit d’un schéma qui se répète pour Elon Musk. Car les gigantesques data centers de xAI à Memphis, baptisés Colossus, tournent déjà quasi exclusivement au gaz naturel avec des dizaines de turbines. Musk a aussi racheté, discrètement et à titre personnel, une entreprise spécialisée dans les turbines mobiles au gaz et au diesel.
Et ce n’est pas tout, puisque SpaceX elle-même a indiqué vouloir acquérir pour 2,8 milliards de dollars de turbines à gaz supplémentaires d’ici à trois ans. Cela ne fait plus vraiment l’ombre d’un doute : Tesla, qui s’est imposée comme pionnière des véhicules électriques et du stockage d’énergie solaire, semble très clairement délaisser ses ambitions initiales. Aujourd’hui, ce sont l’IA et la robotique les priorités.
Un mastodonte industriel
Le gaz naturel n’a pourtant rien d’anodin. À Memphis, les turbines de xAI ont fonctionné pendant des mois sans les permis nécessaires, avant de faire l’objet d’une plainte pour violation du Clean Air Act, la loi fédérale sur la qualité de l’air. En cause, des émissions néfastes dans une zone déjà fortement touchée par la pollution atmosphérique, les riverains faisant part d'une qualité de l’air clairement détériorée qui peut causer des risques accrus d’asthme et de maladies cardiaques.
Mais la machine est en marche, et le projet est vertigineux : 9,29 millions de mètres carrés, soit 929 hectares, d’espace de production sont prévus. L’usine sera entièrement intégrée, avec l’objectif à terme de répondre à une demande de calcul dépassant le térawatt, largement supérieure à l’offre mondiale actuelle.
Les puces produites doivent aussi alimenter les robots Optimus et les Cybercab de Tesla, ainsi que les data centers orbitaux de SpaceX.

articles.title: Indios entrenan a la IA, que los puede remplazar, grabándose con celulares en la cabeza
articles.text:
Miles de personas en India están grabando sus tareas domésticas usando cámaras sujetas a la cabeza para entrenar la próxima generación de robots humanoides.
Esta labor, remunerada con unos dos dólares por hora, ha convertido acciones tan habituales como cortar fruta, doblar ropa o preparar café en material esencial para empresas de tecnología de inteligencia artificial que buscan enseñar a las máquinas a desenvolverse en el mundo real.
PUBLICIDAD
La joven Nagireddy Sriramyachandra, de 25 años, ejemplifica este fenómeno. Con un teléfono móvil atado a la cabeza, se graba a sí misma cortando mangos en la cocina de su casa en Chennai, en el sur de India.
Sus vídeos se envían a compañías tecnológicas globales, interesadas en crear sistemas capaces de imitar los movimientos humanos con naturalidad. “¿Quién más te va a pagar 250 rupias por hora solo por hacer oficio doméstico?”, dijo Sriramyachandra a AFP, quien reconoce que, en un futuro, no descarta tener un robot en casa.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo se entrenan los robots con tareas domésticas en India
El proceso consiste en registrar actividades cotidianas desde la perspectiva de quien las realiza. Las grabaciones, conocidas como “datos egocéntricos”, muestran con precisión cómo se mueven las manos, la manipulación de objetos y la ejecución de acciones simples.
Este material es clave para entrenar modelos de IA especializados que, a diferencia de los chatbots o generadores de imágenes, enfrentan el desafío de interactuar con entornos físicos complejos.
PUBLICIDAD
Algunos entrenadores trabajan desde sus viviendas, mientras otros lo hacen en fábricas o estudios acondicionados con tecnología avanzada: gafas de video, cámaras montadas en la cabeza y sensores de movimiento. Cuando el sistema detecta que las manos no están correctamente visibles, emite un aviso que obliga a repetir la grabación.
Los vídeos se suben a aplicaciones específicas que los canalizan a empresas de análisis de datos, muchas de ellas con presencia en Estados Unidos y clientes entre las principales multinacionales del mundo.
PUBLICIDAD
La demanda de este tipo de datos ha crecido de manera exponencial con el auge de los robots humanoides. Según estimaciones de Morgan Stanley, en 2050 podría haber más de 1.000 millones de estos robots en funcionamiento, sobre todo en sectores industriales y comerciales.
India se ha posicionado como un centro global para la creación, procesamiento y anotación de datos de IA, gracias a la abundancia de mano de obra y a la infraestructura digital en expansión.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué las empresas tecnológicas buscan grabaciones domésticas
Los desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial consideran que alimentar modelos con vídeos en primera persona les permitirá a los robots aprender tareas humanas con mayor realismo. El objetivo es que las máquinas no solo reconozcan imágenes o comandos, sino que puedan replicar movimientos y rutinas complejas, como doblar una toalla, preparar una bebida o colocar etiquetas en productos textiles.
El director de la empresa Objectways, Ravi Shankar, explica que los clientes piden vídeos muy concretos: “Doblar ropa, hacer café, cocinar algo muy específico, hacer sándwiches”. La compañía, con oficinas en India y Estados Unidos, utiliza plataformas como Amazon SageMaker para procesar los datos y trabaja con multinacionales de la lista Fortune 500.
PUBLICIDAD
En una fábrica de textiles de Karur, la rutina es clara: los empleados, con cámaras en la cabeza, planchan bolsas, etiquetan gorras y registran cada paso con precisión.
En otros entornos, como la consultora Qanat en Andhra Pradesh, más de 2.000 colaboradores realizan tareas con sensores en las manos, brazos y piernas. Los datos resultantes no solo sirven para entrenar movimientos, sino que también aportan información sobre la interacción con objetos y la disposición espacial.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál es el impacto social y laboral de entrenar la IA
La expansión de esta economía de datos genera nuevos empleos en India, pero también abre interrogantes sobre el futuro laboral de quienes hoy entrenan a las máquinas. Existen dudas legítimas acerca de si estos trabajadores serán desplazados por los propios sistemas que ayudan a desarrollar.
Las autoridades indias, conscientes del desafío, han encomendado al centro de estudios NITI Aayog la tarea de analizar cómo la IA puede afectar a diferentes sectores, desde zapateros hasta agricultores, y proponen medidas urgentes para evitar una pérdida masiva de empleos, especialmente entre los 490 millones de trabajadores informales del país.
PUBLICIDAD
En los debates públicos y académicos, la atención suele centrarse en las profesiones de “cuello blanco”, anticipando una reducción casi segura de puestos de trabajo en ese segmento. Sin embargo, se ha dedicado poca atención a cómo la inteligencia artificial podría servir a la vasta población informal, que constituye la columna vertebral económica de India.
Ponni, una mujer de 55 años que lleva una década fabricando guirnaldas en la calle en Bangalore, también ha recibido dinero por grabarse mientras trabaja. Advierte que la próxima generación, dedicada a oficios similares, podría enfrentar serios problemas si la automatización avanza sin alternativas laborales.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: El Gobierno ya está retirando gafas para eclipses por riesgos para la vista: cómo comprobar si las tuyas están en la lista
articles.text:
Las gafas para eclipses se han convertido en un bien preciadísimo en el último mes. Muchísimas personas han salido a la calle o a Internet en busca de una protección adecuada para disfrutar del espectáculo astronómico de este miércoles. Pero, como suele ocurrir cuando algo se vende de forma tan masiva, ya ha habido marcas que han tenido que retirar lotes enteros por no estar debidamente fabricados. Es el caso de Lionstar, la compañía que ha tenido que retirar su modelo LSP1, después de que se haya detectado un problema en su filtro de protección.
Un filtro demasiado oscuro para unas gafas para eclipses. El problema de estas gafas no es que no protejan; sino, en cierto modo, que protegen demasiado. Su filtro es tan sumamente oscuro que no se ve nada. Por eso, podemos tener el impulso de mirar por encima de las gafas para no perdernos el espectáculo. Sabemos que ese es un gesto que nos puede dañar las retinas, por eso no pueden permitirse gafas oscuras. No se trata solo de que no se vea nada. Además son peligrosas.
El origen de la alerta. La alerta que ha llevado a la retirada de las gafas para eclipses de Lionstar ha tenido lugar a través de la Red de Alertas del Ministerio de Consumo del Gobierno de España. Inmediatamente se ha procedido a la retirada de estas gafas, que se habían vendido mayormente en farmacias y ópticas online.
Otros casos similares. Otras gafas para eclipses que se han retirado exactamente por problemas de seguridad son el modelo GP0247 de Opticalia, el modelo O37-R, el modelo QW-50Z1 de Homanaje, el lote 2603-01 de la marca ORRO y las gafas de PELISPAN y ECP EYE CARE PROFFESIONAL. En todos los casos, el resultado es el mismo: se han retirado del mercado y se ha advertido a los consumidores para que, en caso de haberlas comprado, no las utilicen.
Si ya has adquirido unas gafas, no se trata de ninguna de estas, pero quieres tener más tranquilidad, puedes comprobar si hay alguna alerta notificada en el buscador del Ministerio de Consumo.
¿Qué pasa si las tienes? En España, si te venden un producto defectuoso, tienes derecho a la devolución del dinero, según el Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2007. Lógicamente, un producto que ha sido retirado por problemas de seguridad, como estas gafas, es más que defectuoso. Por eso, debes ponerte en contacto con el vendedor que te las suministró para proceder a la devolución.
Si optas por no devolverlas, recuerda no usarlas bajo ningún concepto. Básicamente, no vas a ver nada. Aún estás a tiempo de buscar unas gafas debidamente homologadas con la norma EN ISO 12312-2:2015. En cuanto a las gafas defectuosas, si te vas a deshacer de ellas, recuerda separar la montura de cartón del filtro. El cartón va al contenedor azul, el filtro en el gris de restos.

articles.title: Google Chrome change d'interface sur Android pour imposer son bouton Gemini
articles.text:
Google ne cache plus sa volonté d’installer son assistant virtuel Gemini dans les moindres recoins de son écosystème mobile. Après les commandes vocales ou les bulles flottantes d’Android, c’est au tour du navigateur web le plus populaire au monde de lui céder une place de choix. Sur Android, Google Chrome commence à déployer une refonte de son interface pour y intégrer un bouton d’accès direct à Gemini.
Une barre de navigation repensée et plus chargée
Cette nouvelle interface modifie en profondeur l’organisation de l’affichage en adoptant un design dédoublé. La partie supérieure de l’écran regroupe désormais le champ d’adresse URL, un bouton de retour, l’option de partage et le menu principal. La partie inférieure, quant à elle, accueille la gestion des onglets, la création d’une nouvelle page et, au centre de l’attention, le raccourci dédié à Gemini.
 The rollout of Gemini for Chrome on Android has started. I just received this feature in the stable version of Chrome, and as I anticipated, Google has rolled out Gemini along with the new bottom navigation bar:https://t.co/p0xK9Ciyh9 pic.twitter.com/S69BYIO5P6
— Leopeva64 (@Leopeva64) July 14, 2026
Si le déplacement de la barre d’outils en bas de l’écran existe depuis un certain temps pour faciliter l’utilisation à une main sur les grands smartphones, ce nouvel aménagement la rend nettement plus épaisse. L’ensemble crée un affichage plus chargé qui risque de diviser les utilisateurs, mais il permet d’avoir l’intelligence artificielle à portée de pouce à tout moment, un peu à la manière de ce que propose Microsoft avec Copilot sur Edge.
L’IA devient capable d’analyser plusieurs onglets à la fois
Ce raccourci ne se contente pas d’ouvrir une simple fenêtre de discussion. Cette intégration s’accompagne d’un vrai gain de puissance fonctionnel. Jusqu’à présent, l’assistant sur mobile ne pouvait interagir qu’avec la seule page web active affichée à l’écran.
Avec cette mise à jour, Gemini gagne des capacités similaires à sa version latérale sur ordinateur : il devient capable de lire et de croiser les données de plusieurs onglets ouverts simultanément. Vous pouvez ainsi lui demander de comparer deux fiches techniques, de résumer trois articles de presse ou de synthétiser des sources d’information distinctes sans jamais quitter votre navigation.
À lire aussi : Pourquoi Google Chrome exige soudainement 20 Go d’espace libre sur votre PC
Un déploiement progressif au niveau des serveurs
Repérée sur la version stable de Chrome sur Android (v150), cette nouvelle disposition d’interface fait l’objet d’un déploiement progressif géré du côté des serveurs de Google. Tous les utilisateurs ne l’ont donc pas encore reçue simultanément, la firme procédant par vagues successives. Une évolution similaire de l’interface est également attendue dans les prochaines semaines sur l’application Chrome pour iOS.

articles.title: Europe expands its Starlink rival to 348 satellites as IRIS² moves into implementation — €15.6 billion network will boost EU government capacity by 60%, with launches starting in 2029
articles.text:
Europe expands its Starlink rival to 348 satellites as IRIS² moves into implementation — €15.6 billion network will boost EU government capacity by 60%, with launches starting in 2029
66 new satellites are earmarked for defense, security, and emergency services,
The European Commission and the SpaceRISE consortium signed an implementation agreement on Friday, August 7, to roll out Europe’s IRIS² satellite constellation, moving the project from the planning and negotiation stage into full-scale deployment. According to an official press release, the agreement adds 66 satellites to the planned constellation, bringing the total to 348 — 330 satellites in low Earth orbit and 18 in medium Earth orbit — with first launches targeted for 2029.
The expansion is intended to substantially increase the network’s government and defense capacity. According to the Commission, the revised architecture will provide 60% more secure governmental communications capacity within the EU and 54% more globally. The existing satellites in the baseline constellation will also receive additional functionality and stronger security features, while the 66 new spacecraft will operate in higher low Earth orbit.
IRIS² — short for Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity, and Security by Satellite — is the European Union's flagship secure-connectivity constellation, intended to give European governments an autonomous alternative to foreign networks such as SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon's Leo. The Commission signed a 12-year concession contract for the program in December 2024 with the SpaceRISE consortium — a grouping of European satellite operators SES, Eutelsat, and Hispasat — which is building and operating the system under a public-private partnership alongside manufacturers including Airbus Defense and Space, Thales Alenia Space, OHB, and Aerospacelab.
Once operational, the multi-orbit network will deliver sovereign, encrypted connectivity to authorized governmental users across EU member states and participating non-EU countries, currently Norway and Iceland, for use in emergency response, critical infrastructure protection, and security missions, with capacity also earmarked for citizens in areas with poor coverage.
When the concession contract was signed in December 2024, IRIS² carried a price tag of €10.55 billion ($12.19 billion), funded by the European Union, the European Space Agency, and the SpaceRISE consortium. The accelerated timeline and larger constellation have pushed that figure higher, with the consortium's partners now putting total planned investment above €15.6 billion ($18.03 billion), drawn from the EU budget for 2028–2034, ESA, the consortium partners, and member states. Several countries have already committed, with Poland and Hungary pledging €656 million ($758 million) and €500 million ($578 million), respectively, while Spain has announced between €1.6 and €2 billion ($1.85–2.31 billion).
IRIS² is frequently framed as Europe's answer to Starlink, as they are both satellite constellations aimed at providing connectivity to dead zones. However, the primary purpose of the 348-satellite-strong constellation is more niche. The EU wants an independently controlled communications system — mainly for government and emergency use, but also for civilian applications — that can remain available when terrestrial networks fail, or when access to foreign-operated satellite systems becomes politically or strategically uncertain. On the other hand, Starlink’s growing 10,000-satellite constellation is a mainly commercial, privately owned company selling broadband to consumers worldwide. It is now also running satellite-to-phone internet services through Starlink Mobile.

articles.title: Apple Watch mit rundem Display und Whoop-Konkurrent? So sollen Apples Pläne aussehen
articles.text:
Apple Watch mit rundem Display und Whoop-Konkurrent? So sollen Apples Pläne aussehen
In Apples Zubehörabteilung denkt man offenbar über Veränderungen bei der Apple-Watch-Produktlinie nach. Neben neuen Formfaktoren gibt es Pläne für einen Fitness-Tracker ohne integriertes Display, ähnlich wie ihn Anbieter wie Garmin, Fitbit oder Whoop verkaufen. Das hat Bloomberg-Reporter Mark Gurman nach eigenen Angaben von Insidern erfahren.
Schnell dürfte das allerdings nicht gehen: Sowohl das Redesign als auch günstigere Geräte brauchen laut Gurman noch Zeit. Bei den Apple-Watch-Modellen Series 12 und Ultra 4, die im Herbst erscheinen dürften, erwartet er keine radikalen Änderungen bis auf ein verbessertes Innenleben.
Designteam arbeitet an einer „neuen Ära“
Gurman zufolge arbeitet Apple an „revolutionären Designänderungen“ – vergleichbar mit dem iPhone, das im Herbst erstmals als Ultra-Variante mit faltbarem Display kommen soll. Das Industriedesignteam denke die Computeruhr derzeit neu, um ein Gerät für eine „neue Ära“ zu schaffen.
Zu den Optionen gehört eine runde Variante, wie man sie von Samsung kennt. Sicher ist sich Apple dabei aber offenbar noch nicht. Denkbar sind außerdem erneut Premium-Modelle, wie es sie früher als Apple Watch Edition gab. In diesem Zusammenhang soll der Konzern auch über eine Neuauflage eines Keramik-Modells nachdenken, das vor Jahren so eine „Edition“ war.
Darum ein Tracker ohne Display
Geräte von Whoop, Fitbit und anderen Anbietern setzen sich zunehmend durch. Sie zeichnen nur Daten auf und überlassen die Anzeige der App auf dem Smartphone – auch der niedrigere Preis spielt dabei eine Rolle. Diesen Trend nehme Apple „ernst“, schreibt Gurman. Als Fan solcher Geräte gilt Apples Dienstechef Eddy Cue, der inzwischen auch für Apple Health verantwortlich ist.
Er nutzt laut Bericht Produkte von Whoop und Oura – Letzteres ist ein Smart Ring, der Schlaf und Aktivität misst. Auch hier hat Apple angeblich schon lange Pläne, aber nichts Konkretes umgesetzt. Wie lange die Umstellung dauert, ist unklar. Apples Roadmaps erstrecken sich oft über mehrere Jahre. Der Wandel brauche „seine Zeit“, schreibt Gurman.

articles.title: Signed up for Klaviyo? Dozens of advertisers may have seen your password | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Newly revealed security research found that until recently, marketing tech giant Klaviyo was inadvertently sharing the sign-up information of its new customers, including their passwords, with outside advertisers.
Sam Jadali, a security researcher and co-founder of cybersecurity startup Melurna, told TechCrunch that the web form on Klaviyo’s sign-up page was misconfigured between at least February 2024 through November 2025, though likely longer.
The startup’s tests found that anyone who signed up to Klaviyo using the misconfigured form may have had their sign-up information shared with any of the third-party tech giants and advertisers whose trackers are also embedded on the company’s website.
This sign-up data included the customer’s email address and password, as well as their company’s name, website address, and phone number. This information was shared with advertising and tech giants including Facebook and Google; marketing giant HubSpot; Microsoft and its subsidiary LinkedIn; social media site X, and others.
The startup shared its findings with TechCrunch ahead of its talk at the Def Con security conference in Las Vegas.
Klaviyo confirmed to TechCrunch that it fixed the website bug, but questions linger about the incident, including how many people were affected by the data leak over the years. The Boston-based marketing giant allows its 205,000 paying customers to send advertising campaigns across email, text messages, and other channels. Klaviyo’s website says it manages over seven billion customer profiles.
The bug underscores the data risks that third-party trackers can pose to website users when not using defensive tools, like ad-blockers. Klaviyo is the latest company in recent years to have been caught out by inadvertently sharing data with outsiders.
Website trackers, known as “pixels,” allow website and app owners to collect information about their visitors and users, often for understanding how their apps are used and for identifying bugs. These trackers can be misconfigured to also share personal information entered into any web page that they are on.
In the past few years, security lapses stemming from misconfigured pixel trackers have resulted in companies filing data breach disclosures and regulators taking enforcement action.
When reached by TechCrunch, Klaviyo spokesperson Danielle Zanatta confirmed that the bug was related to an “application configuration issue.” Zanatta said the number of known individuals affected was fewer than 200 people, “based on our readily available active logs.” Klaviyo would not say how far back it stores logs, or for how long the bug was active on its website.
Klaviyo said it notified the known individuals affected, but would not provide a copy of the communication that the company allegedly shared with affected customers when asked by TechCrunch.
It’s unclear why the company did not publicly disclose the incident.

articles.title: Info Edge reports 43% rise in net profit for Q1FY27
articles.text:
Info Edge reports 43% rise in net profit for Q1FY27
The Naukri parent saw an 11.4% rise in revenue. Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi attributed recruitment and adoption of AI as key drivers of growth.
Info Edge, the parent company of jobs portal Naukri and real estate platform 99acres, registered a 43% rise in net profit for the first quarter of FY27 while revenue was up 11.4%.
Info Edge reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 490 crore for the first quarter of FY27 as compared to Rs 343 crore registered in the same period a year ago. The revenue during this period stood Rs 881 crore as compared to Rs 490 crore a year ago.
On the performance of the company, Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi said, "Q1FY27 was a stronger quarter relative to the trends we saw through FY26. Recruitment grew well, supported by improving enterprise hiring activity and continued adoption of AI-led offerings such as AI-Rex and Talent Pulse. 99acres continued to strengthen its market leadership and moved closer to breakeven, while Jeevansathi remained profitable during the quarter.”
However, when compared to the fourth quarter of FY26, Info Edge reported a 1.3% rise in revenues and the net profit declined by 35%.
The largest contributor to the revenues of Info Edge came from its recruitment business: Naukri whose topline came in at Rs 630 crore which was a 12% year-on-year (YoY) growth. The real estate business registered a 17% YoY rise to reach a revenue of Rs 130 crore.
However, the gross profitability numbers diverged for both businesses as Naukri reported a profit of Rs 353 crore while for 99acres it was a loss of Rs 2.13 crore.
Info Edge CFO Ambarish Raghuvanshi said, “The company’s cash-generative model was reinforced with cash flows growing by 25.3%. Both recruitment and real estate demonstrated a ramp-up in billings, growing by 17.5% and 16.5%, respectively. All in all, a good quarter.”
The company highlighted that it continues to deepen the use of AI across the group which is enhancing the products and creating new growth opportunities.

articles.title: Fuite de données chez Steam : une cyberattaque compromet les informations des joueurs en Europe
articles.text:
Valve, l’éditeur de Steam, met en garde ses clients européens. Dans un mail adressé aux joueurs, le groupe révèle que CEVA Logistics, le prestataire chargé d’expédier les produits Steam (Steam Deck, Steam Machine, accessoires) aux clients, a été victime d’une cyberattaque.
À lire aussi : Combien coûtera le Steam Frame ? Qualcomm vient de compliquer l’équation
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Entre le 29 juillet et le 1ᵉʳ août 2026, des pirates ont infiltré les systèmes de l’entreprise. Ce ne sont pas les serveurs de Valve qui ont été touchés, mais bien ceux de son sous-traitant logistique, précise bien le mail. Selon les informations communiquées par CEVA à Valve, les hackers ont mis la main sur une partie des données personnelles des clients Steam ayant fait des achats en Europe.
Parmi les informations compromises, on trouve le nom, l’adresse complète, le pays, le numéro de téléphone, l’adresse e-mail associée au compte Steam, ainsi que le type et le prix du matériel commandé. Bonne nouvelle, aucune information de paiement, mot de passe ou code Steam Guard n’est concernée par la fuite de données. Valve précise que CEVA conserve les informations de livraison jusqu’à 90 jours après une commande. C’est pourquoi toutes les personnes qui ont fait une commande sur la période ont été averties de l’incident.
« Certaines informations confidentielles au sujet de la clientèle Steam, y compris les vôtres, ont probablement été compromises », explique Valve dans le courriel.
Une cyberattaque de grande ampleur à l’origine de la fuite
L’attaque à l’encontre de CEVA Logistics s’inscrit dans un piratage plus large ayant frappé huit entrepôts européens du groupe le week-end du 1er août 2026. Les détaillants néerlandais Bol et De Bijenkorf, qui utilisent également les services de CEVA pour expédier des colis, ont émis des alertes similaires au sujet d’une fuite de données. Ces entreprises sont dans la même situation que Steam.
L’Autorité néerlandaise de protection des données personnelles a ouvert une enquête sur l’incident. De son côté, CEVA affirme avoir isolé les systèmes touchés, les avoir mis hors ligne et avoir fait appel à des enquêteurs externes pour évaluer l’ampleur du vol de données.
La fuite fait évidemment planer une menace au-dessus de la tête des joueurs concernés. Ce type de fuite ouvre la porte à des campagnes de phishing ciblées et crédibles. Un escroc disposant du nom, de l’adresse et des détails d’une commande peut se faire passer pour Steam, Valve ou un transporteur afin de réclamer de faux frais de douane, une « confirmation de livraison » ou une connexion sur un faux site pour « vérifier » la commande. C’est pourquoi il faut redoubler de vigilance face aux arnaques aux colis dans les semaines à venir.
Comme le souligne Valve, il n’est pas nécessaire de changer son mot de passe Steam. L’éditeur indique avoir contacté CEVA Logistics pour mieux cerner l’étendue exacte du vol de données. Par ailleurs, Valve affirme être en train de notifier les autorités de protection des données personnelles des pays concernés. En France, Valve va devoir alerter la Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL).

articles.title: Canicule : la France sous 40 degrés à partir du lundi 10 août, voici les départements durement touchés
articles.text:
Canicule : la France sous 40 degrés à partir du lundi 10 août, voici les départements durement touchés
La chaleur repart pour plusieurs jours sur une grande partie de la France. À partir du lundi 10 août 2026, une cinquième vague de chaleur s'installe et montera en puissance à partir de mardi. Météo France attend jusqu'à 40 degrés en milieu de semaine sur presque tout le pays.
Ce lundi 10 août marque le début de ce nouvel épisode que l'on attendait. Les températures reculent d'abord un peu à l'échelle du pays, sauf dans le Sud-Est où elles se maintiennent. Mais ce répit ne dure pas puisque la chaleur repart à la hausse dès le lendemain. Météo France annonce un net réchauffement par le sud à partir du mardi 11 août.
Les prévisions météo de la semaine du 10 août 2026
Dès demain, une 5ème canicule s'abattra sur la France, prolongeant encore la vague de chaleur en cours, sans AUCUN répits pour nos agriculteurs et écosystèmes. Depuis le mois de mai, j'ai sincèrement l'impression que nous vivons désormais sous le climat d'un autre pays.
Les… pic.twitter.com/kZOMUnXNQN
La cinquième canicule de 2026 touche presque toute la France. Du lundi 10 au dimanche 16 août, Météo Paris annonce un écart de 3 à 6 degrés au-dessus des normales de saison. La plupart des grandes villes dépassent 35 degrés à partir de mardi. Un coup de chaud qui remonte du nord de l'Afrique par un flux de sud-ouest, avec un air très chaud sur tout le pays.
Le pic de cette vague arrivera vers le milieu de semaine. Le mercredi 12 août, les valeurs atteindront 40 degrés dans plusieurs régions. Une puissante zone de hautes pressions s'étendra sur le pays et bloque cet air chaud pour plusieurs jours. Dans certains départements, ces fortes chaleurs dureront une grande partie de la semaine.
La canicule saccompagnera de nuits difficiles. Sur toute la période, les minimales dépasseront souvent 20 degrés et le corps sera mis à rude épreuve pour son repos. Le seuil de canicule suppose au moins trois jours de très fortes chaleurs, de jour comme de nuit. Ces conditions seront là dès le mardi sur une large moitié sud.
Pour ce lundi, la vigilance orange concerne 13 départements :
- Ain
- Alpes-Maritimes
- Ardèche
- Corse-du-Sud
- Haute-Corse
- Drôme
- Gard
- Isère
- Rhône
- Savoie
- Haute-Savoie
- Var
- Vaucluse
Une chaleur qui s'accompagne d'une sécheresse
La sécheresse aggrave la situation sur les sols secs. Les orages du début du mois sont tombés de façon très inégale sur ces sols et de nombreux secteurs n'ont pas eu la moindre goutte. Une sécheresse qui atteint un record puisque Dunkerque a enregistré son 39e jour sans pluie, devant l'épisode de 1962. Ces pluies d'orage tombent trop vite pour compenser le manque d'eau.
Dès le dimanche soir, des orages accompagnent ce changement de temps sur le Sud-Ouest, avant la montée des températures. Le Gers, les Hautes-Pyrénées, les Landes et les Pyrénées-Atlantiques passent en vigilance orange orage en fin d'après-midi. La Haute-Garonne, le Lot-et-Garonne, le Tarn et le Tarn-et-Garonne suivent en début de soirée. Sous ces orages, Météo France attend une forte activité électrique et des rafales de 90 à 110 kilomètres par heure.
La cinquième vague confirmera les prévisions d'un été 2026 plus chaud que la normale. Météo France chiffre ce scénario à 70 % pour la période de juillet à septembre. En 2025, l'été a terminé au troisième rang des plus chauds depuis 1900.
